test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 16 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Swachh Vayu Sarvekshan 2025, conducted under the National Clean Air Programme (NCAP), evaluated how many cities across India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**130 cities**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Swachh Vayu Sarvekshan** is an initiative by the **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC)** to rank cities on the basis of implementation of activities approved under the **City Action Plan** and air quality improvement.
 
• Under the **National Clean Air Programme (NCAP)**, the survey for **2025** evaluated **130 cities** across India to measure their progress in reducing air pollution levels.
 
• The assessment is based on various parameters including **solid waste management**, **road dust management**, **management of construction and demolition waste**, **control of vehicular emissions**, and **industrial pollution**.
 
• Cities are ranked based on the self-assessment reports submitted on the **PRANA portal**, which are further vetted by a technical team and third-party agencies.
 
• The **Swachh Vayu Sarvekshan** aims to promote healthy competition among cities and encourage them to take proactive steps toward achieving the targets of the **NCAP**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **National Clean Air Programme (NCAP):**
 
 
• Launched in **January 2019**, the **NCAP** is a long-term, time-bound, national-level strategy to tackle the air pollution problem across the country in a comprehensive manner.
 
• The initial target was to achieve a **20% to 30% reduction** in **Particulate Matter (PM10 and PM2.5)** concentrations by **2024**, keeping **2017** as the base year for comparison.
 
• The **Government of India** later updated the target to achieve a **40% reduction** in particulate matter levels in targeted cities by the year **2026**.
 
 
 
• **Categorization of Cities:**
 
 
• For the purpose of ranking, cities are divided into three categories based on their **2011 Census population**.
 
• **Category 1**: Cities with a population of more than **10 lakhs** (Million-plus cities).
 
• **Category 2**: Cities with a population between **3 lakhs and 10 lakhs**.
 
• **Category 3**: Cities with a population of less than **3 lakhs**.
 
 
 
• **PRANA Portal:**
 
 
• **PRANA** stands for **Portal for Regulation of Air-pollution in Non-Attainment cities**.
 
• It serves as a platform to monitor the implementation of the **NCAP** and provides real-time information on air quality and the status of various city-level action plans.
 
• It facilitates transparency and accountability by allowing the **MoEFCC** and the public to track the progress of **131 non-attainment cities**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Non-Attainment Cities:** These are cities that have consistently failed to meet the **National Ambient Air Quality Standards (NAAQS)** for **PM10** or **Nitrogen Dioxide (NO2)** over a period of **five years**.
 
• **Funding:** The **NCAP** provides dedicated funds to these cities to implement measures like installing **Electric Vehicle (EV)** charging stations, increasing green cover, and upgrading mechanical street sweeping machines.
 
• **Incentives:** Cities performing well in the **Swachh Vayu Sarvekshan** are awarded **cash prizes** and trophies to further motivate local urban bodies to prioritize **environmental health**.
 
• **Air Quality Index (AQI):** While the Sarvekshan looks at action taken, the **AQI** remains the standard daily tool for communicating the health of the air to the public, ranging from **'Good' (0-50)** to **'Severe' (above 400)**.
